concepts.def: Hierarchical division of society into ranked groups based on power, wealth and status.
Davis and Moore (1945): inequality is necessary to motivate the most talented into the most important roles.
Society polarised into bourgeoisie (own means of production) and proletariat (sell labour); class conflict drives history.
Stratification involves class (economic), status (prestige) and party (power); more nuanced than Marx.
Weber's term for opportunities to gain valued resources (health, education, income) shaped by social position.
Measure of income inequality from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (one person has all); UK around 0.36 (ONS).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Social Differentiation & Stratification — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Social Differentiation & Stratification brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Social Differentiation & Stratification.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Necessary to motivate talent
A capitalist conspiracy
Disappearing

mcqs.q: What is the postmodern view of identity?
options: Identity is fixed by class, gender, and ethnicity at birth.
Identities are fluid, fragmented, and constructed through consumption and choice.
Because crime makes society wealthier.
Everyone has the same identity in postmodern society.
